    #Longitudinal Static Stability

    Criteria for longitudinal static stability,

    dαdCm​​≡Cmα​​<0 (Negative gradient)

    dCL​dCm​​≡CmCL​​​<0 (Negative gradient)

    Cm0​​>0 (Positive y-intercept)

    Relations between angle of attack,

    αFRL​=αw​−iw​

    αabsw​​=αw​−α0w​​

    αt​=αFRL​−ε+it​

    Longitudinal static stability curve,

    Cm​=dαdCm​​α+Cmα=0​​

    Cm​=dCL​dCm​​CL​+CmL=0​​

    #Contribution of Components

    #Wing Contribution

    Coefficient of wing pitch moment,

    Cmw​​=Cmacw​​​+CLw​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Note that CLw​​=CL0w​​​+CLαw​​​αw​.

    Coefficient of wing pitch moment,

    Cmw​​=Cm0w​​​+Cmαw​​​αw​

    Cm0w​​​=Cmacw​​​+CL0w​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Cmαw​​​=CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Linear form of equation

    #Horizontal Tail Contribution

    Horizontal tail efficiency,

    ηH​=21​ρVw​221​ρVt​2​

    Horizontal tail volume ratio,

    VH​=cˉlt​​Sw​St​​

    where lt​ is the distance of tail ac from the CG

    Coefficient of tail pitch moment,

    Cmt​​=−ηH​VH​CLt​​

    Coefficient of tail pitch moment,

    Cmt​​=Cm0t​​​+Cmαt​​​αw​

    Cm0t​​​=ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(ε0​+iw​−it​)

    Cmαt​​​=−ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(1−dαdε​)

    where tail lift slope CLαt​​​=1+a0​/(πeAR)a0​​

    Downwash angle equation,

    ε=ε0​+dαdε​αw​

    where ε0​ is downwash angle at αw​=0

    #Total Pitching Moment

    Coefficient of total pitch moment,

    Cm​=Cmw​​+Cmt​​+Cmf​​

    Coefficient of total pitch moment,

    Cm​=Cm0​​+Cm(αw​)​​(αw​)

    Cm0​​=Cmacw​​​+CL0w​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)+ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(ε0​+iw​−it​)+Cm0f​​​

    Cm(αw​)​​=CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)−ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(1−dαdε​)+Cmαf​​​

    Equation expressed in terms of wing angle of attack.

    Coefficient of total pitch moment,

    Cm​=Cm0​​+Cmα​​α

    Cm0​​=Cmacw​​​+(CL0w​​​+CLαw​​​iw​)(cˉxCG​−xac​​)            +ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(ε0​+dαdε​iw​−it​)+Cm0f​​​+Cmαf​​​iw​

    Cmα​​=CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)−ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(1−dαdε​)+Cmαf​​​

    Equation expressed in terms of aircraft (fuselage) angle of attack.

    Coefficient of total pitch moment,

    Cm​=Cm0​​+Cmα​​α

    Cm​=Cm0​​+dαabs​dCm​​αabs​

    Cm​=Cm0​​+(dCL​dCm​​⋅dαabs​dCL​​)αabs​

    Cm​=Cm0​​+dCL​dCm​​(CLαabs​​​αabs​)

    Cm​=Cm0​​+CmCL​​​CL​

    #Static Margin

    Location of neutral point where Cmα​​=0,

    0=CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)−ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(1−dαdε​)+Cmαf​​​

    cˉxNP​​=cˉxac​​−CLαw​​​Cmαf​​​​+ηH​VH​CLαw​​​CLαt​​​​(1−dαdε​)

    Static margin (stick-fixed),

    SM=cˉxNP​​−cˉxCG​​=−CLαw​​​Cmα​​​=−dCL​dCm​​

    Cmα​​ is the trim curve slope of Cm​ vs α.

    CLαw​​​ is the lift curve slope of CL​ vs α.

    For longitudinal static stability, SM>0.

    #Maneuver Margin

    Relative density parameter,

    μ=ρglt​SW​

    Maneuver margin,

    MM=SM+2μηH​VH​CLαt​​​​=−dCL​d(CmCG​​)m​​

    Location of maneuver point,

    MM=cˉxNP​​−cˉxCG​​+2μηH​VH​CLαt​​​​

    0=cˉxNP​​−cˉxMP​​+2μηH​VH​CLαt​​​​

    cˉxMP​​=cˉxNP​​+2μηH​VH​CLαt​​​​

    Note that CLαt​​​ is expressed in per radian.

    #Longitudinal Control

    #Elevator Control

    Elevator effectiveness,

    ae​=dδe​dCLt​​​=dαt​dCLt​​​dδe​dαt​​=dαt​dCLt​​​τ

    where τ is elevator flap effectiveness

    Aircraft lift coefficient vs elevator deflection,

    CLδe​​​=ηH​SSt​​dδe​dCLt​​​=ηH​SSt​​ae​

    where ηH​ is horizontal tail efficiency

    Elevator control power,

    Cmδe​​​=dδe​dCm​​=−ηH​VH​ae​

    #Pitching Control

    Total pitching moment (with elevator deflection),

    Cm​=Cmα=0​​+Cmα​​α+Cmδe​​​δe​

    Cm​=CmL=0​​+dCL​dCm​​CL​+Cmδe​​​δe​

    #Elevator Angle to Trim

    Elevator deflection (in trim condition),

    δetrim​​=−Cmδe​​​Cm0​​+Cmα​​αtrim​​

    δetrim​​=−Cmδe​​​Cm0​​​−Cmδe​​​dCm​/dCL​​CLtrim​​

    δetrim​​=−Cmδe​​​Cm0​​​+Cmδe​​​SM​CLtrim​​

    δetrim​​=δetrim0​​​+dCLtrim​​dδetrim​​​CLtrim​​

    Most forward location of CG when trimmed at CLmax​​,

    cˉxCGf​​​=cˉxNP​​−(δemin​​+Cmδe​​​Cm0​​​)CLmax​​Cmδe​​​​

    Most aft location of CG at minimum static margin,

    SMmin​=cˉxNP​​−cˉxCGa​​​

    Minimum static margin is typically 0.05.

    Range of allowable CG locations,

    ΔxˉCG​=cˉxCGa​​​−cˉxCGf​​​

    #Directional & Lateral

    #Directional Static Stability

    Criterion for directional static stability,

    dβdCn​​=Cnβ​>0

    Positive yaw to counter positive sideslip.

    Coefficient of yaw moment,

    Cn​=21​ρV2SbN​

    #Wing-Fuselage Contribution

    Coefficient of yaw moment,

    Cnβwf​​=−kn​kRI​SbSfs​lf​​

    where Sfs​ is the projected side area,
    and     lf​ is the fuselage length

    #Vertical Tail Contribution

    Coefficient of tail yaw moment,

    Cnβvt​​=dβdCnvt​​​

    Cnβvt​​=Vvt​ηvt​CLαvt​​​(1+dβdσ​)

    where dβdσ​ is the sidewash factor

    #Lateral Static Stability

    Criterion for lateral static stability,

    dβdCl​​=Clβ​<0

    Negative roll to counter positive sideslip.

    #Vertical Tail Contribution

    Coefficient of tail roll moment,

    Clβvt​​=−lvt​zvt​​Cnβvt​​

    where zvt​ is the height of tail ac from FRL,
    and     lvt​ is the distance of tail ac from CG

    #Rudder Control

    Change in yaw moment due to rudder deflection,

    ΔCnδr​​​=−ηvt​Vvt​dδr​dCLvt​​​δr​

    Rudder effectiveness and control power,

    Cnδr​​​=−ηvt​Vvt​dδr​dCLvt​​​

    Cnδr​​​=−ηvt​Vvt​(dαvt​dCLvt​​​⋅dδr​dαvt​​)

    Cnδr​​​=−ηvt​Vvt​CLαvt​​​τ

    where τ is rudder flap effectiveness

    #Directional-Lateral Coupling

    #Crosswind Landing

    0=Clβ​β+Clδa​​​δa​+Clδr​​​δr​

    0=Cnβ​β+Cnδa​​​δa​+Cnδr​​​δr​

    0=CYβ​β+CYδa​​​δa​+CYδr​​​δr​+21​ρV∞​2SWsinϕ​

    where Wsinϕ≡ lateral weight component due to banking

    #Crabbed Approach

    Implied conditions:

    • β=0° (Aircraft flies into relative wind)
    • δr​=0°   δa​=0°   ϕ=0° (Solution)

    #Sideslip Approach

    Implied conditions:

    • β=tan−1V∞​v​ (Aircraft flies at a fixed sideslip angle)

    #Single Engine Failure during Flight

    Aircraft wheels have not touched the ground.

    0=Clβ​β+Clδr​​​δr​+Clδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SbLE​​

    0=Cnβ​β+Cnδr​​​δr​+Cnδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SbNE​​

    0=CYβ​β+CYδr​​​δr​+CYδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SWsinϕ​

    where LE​≡ roll moment due to engine failure,
    and     NE​≡ yaw moment due to engine failure

    Implied conditions:

    • β=0° (To maintain same heading and if there is no crosswind)
    • ϕ=0° (To maintain wings-level fight with no banking)
    • Calculated δr​ and δa​ must be within deflection limits
    • For landing approach ϕ<5° (Ground clearance)

    #Single Engine Failure during Ground Run

    Aircraft wheels have touched the ground.

    0=Clβ​β+Clδr​​​δr​+Clδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SbLE​​

    0=Cnβ​β+Cnδr​​​δr​+Cnδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SbNE​​

    21​ρV∞​2SY​=CYβ​β+CYδr​​​δr​+CYδa​​​δa​+21​ρV∞​2SWsinϕ​

    where Y≡ unbalanced side force of the rudder

    Ground friction,

    fr=μ(W−L)

    If Y<fr, aircraft will not skid.
    If     Y>fr, aircraft will skid.

    Implied conditions:

    • β=0° (Aircraft’s motion is along the runway centerline)
    • ϕ=0° (Aircraft is on the ground and cannot bank)
    • LE​≈0 (Small compared to yawing moment)

    #6-DOF Modelling of Aircraft

    Euler angles:

    • Yaw rotation −π≤ψ≤π
    • Pitch rotation −2π​≤θ≤2π​
    • Roll rotation −π≤ϕ≤π

    Euler rates (ψ˙​, θ˙, ϕ˙​) are rotational rates about zi​, y1​, and x2​ axes respectively.

    • ψ˙​ is measured in the inertial frame (inertia axis i → 1 → 2 → body-fixed axis b)
    • θ˙ is measured in frame 1 (1 → 2 → body-fixed axis b)
    • ϕ˙​ is measured in frame 2 (2 → body-fixed axis b)

    #Rotation Matrices

    Convert from inertia axis i → single-axis 1,

    ⎩⎨⎧​x1​y1​z1​​⎭⎬⎫​=​cosψ−sinψ0​sinψcosψ0​001​​⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​=Tψ​⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​

    Note that Tψ​≡T1i​≡ yaw rotation matrix.

    Convert from single-axis 1 → two-axis 2,

    ⎩⎨⎧​x2​y2​z2​​⎭⎬⎫​=​cosθ0sinθ​010​−sinθ0cosθ​​⎩⎨⎧​x1​y1​z1​​⎭⎬⎫​=Tθ​⎩⎨⎧​x1​y1​z1​​⎭⎬⎫​

    Note that Tθ​≡T21​≡ pitch rotation matrix.

    Convert from two-axis 2 → body-fixed axis b,

    ⎩⎨⎧​xb​yb​zb​​⎭⎬⎫​=​100​0cosϕ−sinϕ​0sinϕcosϕ​​⎩⎨⎧​x2​y2​z2​​⎭⎬⎫​=Tϕ​⎩⎨⎧​x2​y2​z2​​⎭⎬⎫​

    Note that Tϕ​≡Tb,2​≡ roll rotation matrix.

    #Transformation Matrices

    Convert from inertia axis → body-fixed axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​xb​yb​zb​​⎭⎬⎫​=Tϕ​Tθ​Tψ​⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​=Tb2​T21​T1i​⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​

    ⎩⎨⎧​xb​yb​zb​​⎭⎬⎫​=​Cθ​Cψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Cψ​−Cϕ​Sψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Cψ​+Sϕ​Sψ​​Cθ​Sψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Sψ​+Cϕ​Cψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Sψ​−Sϕ​Cψ​​−Sθ​Sϕ​Cθ​Cϕ​Cθ​​​⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​

    where C≡cos and S≡sin

    Convert from body-fixed axis → inertia axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​xi​yi​zi​​⎭⎬⎫​=​Cθ​Cψ​Cθ​Sψ​−Sθ​​Sϕ​Sθ​Cψ​−Cϕ​Sψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Sψ​+Cϕ​Cψ​Sϕ​Cθ​​Cϕ​Sθ​Cψ​+Sϕ​Sψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Sψ​−Sϕ​Cψ​Cϕ​Cθ​​​⎩⎨⎧​xb​yb​zb​​⎭⎬⎫​

    where Tib​=(Tbi​)−1=(Tbi​)T=(Tϕ​Tθ​Tψ​)T=(Tψ​)T(Tθ​)T(Tϕ​)T

    #Linear Velocity Transformation

    Convert from inertia axis → body-fixed axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​uvw​⎭⎬⎫​=​Cθ​Cψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Cψ​−Cϕ​Sψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Cψ​+Sϕ​Sψ​​Cθ​Sψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Sψ​+Cϕ​Cψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Sψ​−Sϕ​Cψ​​−Sθ​Sϕ​Cθ​Cϕ​Cθ​​​⎩⎨⎧​x˙i​y˙​i​z˙i​​⎭⎬⎫​

    Convert from body-fixed axis → inertia axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​x˙i​y˙​i​z˙i​​⎭⎬⎫​=​Cθ​Cψ​Cθ​Sψ​−Sθ​​Sϕ​Sθ​Cψ​−Cϕ​Sψ​Sϕ​Sθ​Sψ​+Cϕ​Cψ​Sϕ​Cθ​​Cϕ​Sθ​Cψ​+Sϕ​Sψ​Cϕ​Sθ​Sψ​−Sϕ​Cψ​Cϕ​Cθ​​​⎩⎨⎧​uvw​⎭⎬⎫​

    #Angular Velocity Transformation

    Convert from inertia axis → body-fixed axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​pqr​⎭⎬⎫​=​100​0cosϕ−sinϕ​−sinθsinϕcosθcosϕcosθ​​⎩⎨⎧​ϕ˙​θ˙ψ˙​​⎭⎬⎫​

    where p≡ roll rate, q≡ pitch rate, and r≡ yaw rate

    Convert from body-fixed axis → inertia axis,

    ⎩⎨⎧​ϕ˙​θ˙ψ˙​​⎭⎬⎫​=​100​sinϕtanθcosϕsinϕsecθ​cosϕtanθ−sinϕcosϕsecθ​​⎩⎨⎧​pqr​⎭⎬⎫​

    #Aircraft Equations of Motion (EoM)

    General equation for total time derivative,

    (dtdA​)inertia​=(dtdA​)rotating​+ω×A

    where ω is the angular velocity vector of the rotating frame (body)

    Linear momentum of aircraft,

    L=mV=m(ui^b​+vj^​b​+wk^b​)

    Angular momentum of aircraft,

    H=(pIxx​−rIxz​)i^b​+(qIyy​)j^​b​+(−pIxz​+rIzz​)k^b​

    External forces acting on the aircraft,

    Fext​=ma=dtd​mV=dtd​L

    Fext​=(dtdL​)b​+ω×L

    X=m(u˙+qw−rv)Y=m(v˙+ru−pw)Z=m(w˙+pv−qu)

    External moments acting on the aircraft,

    Mext​=Iα=dtd​Iω=dtd​H

    Mext​=(dtdH​)b​+ω×H

    L=Ixx​p˙​−Ixz​r˙+(Izz​−Iyy​)qr−Ixz​pqM=Iyy​q˙​+(Ixx​−Izz​)pr+Ixz​(p2−r2)N=−Ixz​p˙​+Izz​r˙+(Iyy​−Ixx​)pq+Ixz​qr

    #Linear Systems Theory

    #Linearization

    Steps to linearizing:

    • Solve for equilibrium/operating points by setting f(x)=0
    • Take small variations around the equilibrium point x=x0​+Δx
    • Linearize the equation by substituting the above into the original equation

    Single-variable system,

    Δx˙=f′(x0​)Δx=AΔx

    Multi-variable system,

    ΔX˙=∂X∂F​​X0​​ΔX=AΔX

    Jacobian matrix,

    A=∂X∂F​​X0​​=​∂f1​/∂x1​∂f2​/∂x1​⋮∂fn​/∂x1​​∂f1​/∂x2​∂f2​/∂x2​⋮∂fn​/∂x2​​……⋱…​∂f2​/∂xn​∂f2​/∂xn​⋮∂fn​/∂xn​​​

    Stability of a system (eigenvalues and eigenvectors):

    • Solve for the roots of the characteristic equation ∣A−λI∣=0
    • System is stable if all of its eigenvalues are negative λn​<0
    • Substitute eigenvalue into matrix to obtain eigenvectors

    #First-Order System (Spring-Damper)

    Transfer function,

    T(s)=F(s)X(s)​=cs+k1​

    Total response of the system,

    X(s)=cs+kF(s)​+cs+kcx0​​

    X(s)=T(s)⋅F(s)+T(s)⋅cx0​

    1st term represents the forced response.
    2nd term represents the free response.

    Free response of the system,

    x(t)=x0​es1​t=x0​e−t/τ

    where time constant τ=−s1​1​=kc​

    Forced response to step input,

    x(t)=kF0​​(1−e−t/τ)

    where kF0​​=x∞​ when t→∞

    #Second-Order System (Mass-Spring-Damper)

    Transfer function,

    T(s)=F(s)X(s)​=ms2+cs+k1​=k1​⋅s2+2ζωn​s+ωn​2ωn​2​

    Characteristic equation of the system,

    CE=ms2+cs+k

    If c2−4mk>0, the system is overdamped (two distinct real poles).
    If     c2−4mk<0, the system is underdamped (two complex poles).
    If     c2−4mk=0, the system is critically damped (two repeated poles).

    Natural frequency of a system,

    ωn​=mk​​

    Critical damping constant of a system,

    ccr​=2km​=2mωn​=ωn​2k​

    Damping ratio of a system,

    ζ=ccr​c​=2km​c​=2mωn​c​=2k/ωn​c​

    Total response of the system,

    X(s)=ms2+cs+kF(s)​+ms2+cs+k(ms+c)x0​+mx˙0​​

    X(s)=T(s)⋅F(s)+T(s)[(ms+c)x0​+mx˙0​]

    1st term represents the forced response.
    2nd term represents the free response.

    Forced response to step input, overdamped ζ>1,

    x(t)=kF0​​[1+2ζ2−1​ωn​​(s1​es1​t​+s2​es2​t​)]

    Forced response to step input, underdamped 0<ζ<1,

    x(t)=kF0​​[1−1−ζ2​e−ζωn​t​sin(ωd​t+ϕ)]

    where tanϕ=ζωn​ωd​​=ζ1−ζ2​​

    Rise time,

    tr​=ωd​π−ϕ​=ωn​1−ζ2​π−ϕ​

    Peak time,

    tp​=ωd​π​=ωn​1−ζ2​π​

    Percent overshoot,

    Mp​=e1−ζ2​−ζπ​×100%

    ±2% settling time,

    ts(2%)​=ζωn​4​

    ±5% settling time,

    ts(5%)​=ζωn​3​

    Forced response to step input, critically damped ζ=1,

    x(t)=kF0​​[1−e−ζωn​t(1+ωn​t)]

    Forced response to step input, undamped ζ=0,

    x(t)=kF0​​[1−cos(ωn​t)]

    #Routh-Hurwitz Criterion

    Stability of a system:

    • System is unstable if there is a sign change in the 1st column
    • Number of sign changes → number of poles with positive real parts

    Zero in the 1st Column

    If the first element of a row is zero:

    • Replace the zero with ε
    • ε is allowed to approach zero from either the positive or negative side
    • Determinants are expressed in terms of ε and signs of each element is determined

    Entire Row is Zeroes

    If the entire row is zeroes:

    • Form auxiliary polynomial using elements in the row above it as coefficients
    • Differentiate the auxiliary polynomial with respect to s
    • Replace the zeroes with coefficients of the derivative

    #Steady-State Error

    Initial value theorem,

    f(0+)=t→0+lim​ f(t)=s→∞lim​ sF(s)

    Final value theorem,

    f(∞)=t→∞lim​ f(t)=s→0lim​ sF(s)

    Closed-loop transfer function,

    M(s)=R(s)C(s)​=1+G(s)⋅H(s)G(s)​

    If the feedback loop is positive, the sign in the denominator is “+”.

    Steady-state error (negative unity feedback),

    e(∞)=t→∞lim​ e(t)=s→0lim​ sE(s)=s→0lim​ 1+G(s)sR(s)​

    whereby R(s) is the Laplace transform of the input

    #Linearization of Aircraft EoM

    #Nomenclature

    • Axial velocity u
    • Lateral velocity v
    • Normal velocity w
    • Roll rate p
    • Pitch rate q
    • Yaw rate r
    • Axial force X
    • Side force Y
    • Normal force Z
    • Roll moment L
    • Pitch moment M
    • Yaw moment N

    • Angle of attack α≈uw​
    • Sideslip angle β≈uv​≈Vv​
    • Axial velocity u=Vcosβcosα
    • Lateral velocity v=Vsinβ
    • Normal velocity w=Vcosβsinα

    #Reference Flight Condition

    Small disturbance in angle of attack
    due to incremental normal velocity,

    Δα≈u0​Δw​

    α=α0​+Δα

    θ=θ0​−Δα

    Small disturbance in angle of attack
    due to incremental pitch angle,

    Δα=Δθ

    α=α0​+Δα

    θ=θ0​+Δθ

    #Linearized Equations

    Longitudinal Motion

    Axial force equation,

    Δu˙=Xu​Δu+Xw​Δw+Xδe​​Δδe​+XδT​​ΔδT​−g(cosθ0​)Δθ

    Normal force equation,

    (1−Zw˙​)Δw˙=Zu​Δu+Zw​Δw+(Zq​+u0​)Δq                           +Zδe​​Δδe​+ZδT​​ΔδT​−g(sinθ0​)Δθ

    Pitching moment equation,

    Δq˙​=Mu​Δu+Mw​Δw+Mw˙​Δw˙+Mq​Δq+Mδe​​Δδe​+MδT​​ΔδT​

    Lateral-Directional Motion

    Side force equation,

    Δv˙=Yv​Δv+Yp​Δp+(Yr​−u0​)Δr+Yδr​​Δδr​+g(cosθ0​)Δϕ

    Rolling moment equation,

    Δp˙​−Ixx​Ixz​​Δr˙=Lv​Δv+Lp​Δp+Lr​Δr+Lδa​​Δδa​+Lδr​​Δδr​

    Yawing moment equation,

    Δr˙−Izz​Ixz​​Δp˙​=Nv​Δv+Np​Δp+Nr​Δr+Nδa​​Δδa​+Nδr​​Δδr​

    #Aircraft Dynamics

    #Longitudinal Dynamics

    #Long Period Approximation

    Assumptions:

    • Pitching moment equation Δq˙​=… is neglected
    • Change in angle of attack Δα≈0 such that normal velocity Δw≈0
    • Normal force derivative Zq​≈0 such that initial aircraft velocity u0​≫Zq​
    • Aircraft is initially in level flight where θ0​=0 (small angle approximation)

    Axial force and normal force equations simplify to,

    {Δu˙Δθ˙​}=[Xu​−u0​Zu​​​−g0​]{ΔuΔθ​}

    0=λ2−Xu​λ−u0​Zu​g​

    Natural frequency of oscillation,

    ωn,phu​=−u0​Zu​g​​=2​u0​g​

    Damping ratio of oscillation,

    ζphu​=−2ωnphu​​Xu​​=2​1​L/D1​

    #Short Period Approximation

    Assumptions:

    • Axial force equation Δu˙=…  is neglected
    • Change in aircraft velocity Δu≈0
    • Zq​≪u0​ and Zw˙​≪1
    • Aircraft is initially in level flight where θ0​=0 (small angle approximation)

    Normal force and pitching moment equations simplify to,

    {Δα˙Δq˙​​}=[u0​Zα​​Mα​+Mα˙​u0​Zα​​​1Mα˙​+Mq​​]{ΔαΔq​}

    0=λ2−(Mα˙​+Mq​+u0​Zα​​)λ+(Mq​u0​Zα​​−Mα​)

    Natural frequency of oscillation,

    ωn,spo​=Mq​u0​Zα​​−Mα​​

    Damping ratio of oscillation,

    ζspo​=2ωnspo​​−(Mα˙​+Mq​+Zα​/u0​)​

    #1-DOF Approximation to Pure Pitching Motion

    Simplifications and substitutions:

    • Change in aircraft velocity Δu=0
    • Δα=Δθ=u0​Δw​
    • Δα˙=Δθ˙=Δq

    From Newton’s 2nd law,

    Iyy​Δθ¨=ΔMCG​

    Iyy​Δθ¨=∂α∂M​Δα+∂α˙∂M​Δα˙+∂q∂M​Δq+∂δe​∂M​Δδe​

    Iyy​Δθ¨=∂α∂M​Δα+(∂α˙∂M​+∂q∂M​)Δα˙+∂δe​∂M​Δδe​

    Δθ¨=Iyy​1​∂α∂M​Δα+Iyy​1​(∂α˙∂M​+∂q∂M​)Δα˙+Iyy​1​∂δe​∂M​Δδe​

    Δα¨=Mα​Δα+(Mα˙​+Mq​)Δα˙+Mδe​​Δδe​

    Mδe​​Δδe​=Δα¨−(Mα˙​+Mq​)Δα˙−Mα​Δα

    Equation is a 2nd-order non-homogeneous ODE.

    In dynamic stability analysis, elevator input is zero.

    0=Δα¨−(Mα˙​+Mq​)Δα˙−Mα​Δα

    Equation is a 2nd-order homogeneous ODE.

    Natural frequency of motion,

    ωn,pitch​=−Mα​​

    Damping ratio of motion,

    ζpitch​=2ωnpitch​​−(Mα˙​+Mq​)​

    Pitching Response to Step Elevator Input

    Response of a 2nd-order system to a step input,

    Δα(t)=Δαtrim​[1−1−ζ2​1​e−ζωn​tsin(ωd​t+ϕ)]

    where desired change in trim angle of attack Δαtrim​=−Mα​Mδe​​​Δδe​

    #Lateral-Directional Dynamics

    #Spiral Mode Approximation

    Assumptions:

    • Side force equation Δv˙=… is neglected
    • Negligible roll rate Δp≈0
    • Negligible moments of inertia Ixx​Ixz​​≈0 and Izz​Ixz​​≈0

    Rolling and yawing moment equations simplify to,

    0=Lβ​Δβ+Lr​Δr

    Δr˙=Nβ​Δβ+Nr​Δr

    Combining both equations,

    0=Δr˙+Lβ​Lr​Nβ​−Lβ​Nr​​Δr

    0=λ+Lβ​Lr​Nβ​−Lβ​Nr​​

    For a stable spiral mode,

    λspiral​=−Lβ​Lr​Nβ​−Lβ​Nr​​<0

    Time constant of spiral mode,

    τ=−s1​1​=−λspiral​1​

    #Dutch Roll Approximation

    Assumptions:

    • Rolling moment equation Δp˙​=… is neglected
    • Negligible rolling motion such that Δp=0 and Δϕ=0
    • Negligible moments of inertia Ixx​Ixz​​≈0 and Izz​Ixz​​≈0

    Side force and yawing moment equations simplify to,

    {Δβ˙​Δr˙​}=[u0​Yβ​​Nβ​​u0​Yr​​−1Nr​​]{ΔβΔr​}

    0=λ2−u0​Yβ​+u0​Nr​​λ+u0​Yβ​Nr​−Yr​Nβ​+u0​Nβ​​

    Natural frequency of Dutch roll,

    ωn,DR​=u0​Yβ​Nr​−Yr​Nβ​+u0​Nβ​​​

    Damping ratio of Dutch roll,

    ζDR​=−2u0​ωn,DR​Yβ​+u0​Nr​​

    #1-DOF Approximation to Pure Rolling Motion

    From Newton’s 2nd law,

    Ixx​Δϕ¨​=ΔLCG​

    Ixx​Δp˙​=∂p∂L​Δp+∂δa​∂L​Δδa​

    Δp˙​=Ixx​1​∂p∂L​Δp+Ixx​1​∂δa​∂L​Δδa​

    Δp˙​=Lp​Δp+Lδa​​Δδa​

    Lδa​​Δδa​=Δp˙​−Lp​Δp

    Equation is a 1st-order ODE.

    Roots of characteristic equation,

    λroll​=Lp​

    Time constant of motion,

    τ=−s1​1​=−Lp​1​

    Rewriting the equation,

    Lδa​​Δδa​=Δp˙​−Lp​Δp

    −Lp​Lδa​​​Δδa​=−Lp​1​Δp˙​+Δp

    −Lp​Lδa​​​Δδa​=τΔp˙​+Δp

    Solution to 1st-order ODE,

    Δp(t)=−Lp​Lδa​​​Δδa​(1−e−t/τ)

    Steady-state solution to 1st-order ODE,

    Δpss​=−Lp​Lδa​​​Δδa​

    #1-DOF Approximation to Pure Yawing Motion

    From Newton’s 2nd law,

    Izz​Δψ¨​=ΔNCG​

    Izz​Δψ¨​=∂β∂N​Δβ+∂r∂N​Δr+∂δr​∂N​Δδr​

    Δψ¨​=Izz​1​∂β∂N​Δβ+Izz​1​∂r∂N​Δr+Izz​1​∂δr​∂N​Δδr​

    Note that ψ=−β.

    In terms of sideslip angle,

    Δψ¨​=Nβ​Δβ+Nr​Δψ˙​+Nδr​​Δδr​

    −Δβ¨​=Nβ​Δβ−Nr​Δβ˙​+Nδr​​Δδr​

    −Nδr​​Δδr​=Δβ¨​−Nr​Δβ˙​+Nβ​Δβ

    In terms of yaw angle,

    Δψ¨​=Nβ​Δβ+Nr​Δψ˙​+Nδr​​Δδr​

    Δψ¨​=−Nβ​Δψ+Nr​Δψ˙​+Nδr​​Δδr​

    Nδr​​Δδr​=Δψ¨​−Nr​Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Equation is a 2nd-order non-homogeneous ODE.

    Natural frequency of motion,

    ωn,yaw​=Nβ​​

    Damping ratio of motion,

    ζyaw​=−2ωn,yaw​Nr​​

    Solution to 2nd-order ODE,

    Δβ(t)=Δβtrim​[1−1−ζ2​e−ζωn​t​sin(ωd​t+ϕ)]

    where tanϕ=ζωn​ωd​​=ζ1−ζ2​​

    Desired change in trim sideslip angle,

    Δβtrim​=−Nβ​Nδr​​​Δδr​

    #Yaw Damper

    With Yaw Rate Feedback

    Feedback of system,

    (Δδr​)feedback​=kΔψ˙​

    Yawing motion equation with feedback,

    Nδr​​Δδr​+Nδr​​(Δδr​)feedback​=Δψ¨​−Nr​Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Nδr​​Δδr​+kNδr​​Δψ˙​=Δψ¨​−Nr​Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Nδr​​Δδr​=Δψ¨​−(Nr​−kNδr​​)Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Equation is a 2nd-order non-homogeneous ODE.

    Natural frequency remains unchanged,

    ωn,yaw​=Nβ​​

    Damping ratio is altered,

    ζyaw damper​=−2ωn,yaw​Nr​+kNδr​​​

    With Yaw Rate and Yaw Angle Feedback

    Feedback of system,

    (Δδr​)feedback​=k1​Δψ˙​+k2​Δψ

    Yawing motion equation with feedback,

    Nδr​​Δδr​+Nδr​​(Δδr​)feedback​=Δψ¨​−Nr​Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Nδr​​Δδr​+k1​Nδr​​Δψ˙​+k2​Nδr​​Δψ=Δψ¨​−Nr​Δψ˙​+Nβ​Δψ

    Nδr​​Δδr​=Δψ¨​−(Nr​+k1​Nδr​​)Δψ˙​+(Nβ​−k2​Nδr​​)Δψ

    Equation is a 2nd-order non-homogeneous ODE.

    Natural frequency is altered,

    ωn,yaw damper​=Nβ​−k2​Nδr​​​

    Damping ratio is altered,

    ζyaw damper​=−2ωn,yaw damper​Nr​+k1​Nδr​​​
